scenario: [RFCS.16.3]: field 260 is `reserved` in `proto/atom.proto`; no runtime names it. A stream carrying an atom at 260 is read as it reads any unknown skip-band number: the atom is skipped by its length and every atom after it decodes. LFST.2.2's session -- one Reading asserted, no pump -- is recorded by each runtime's own writer, an atom at 260 is spliced in after the StreamHeader ([RCTS.1.2.20]'s `splice_field`), and the stream is decoded. The known atoms are exactly LFST.2.2's, with no Seal among them. A reader naming 260 decodes the spliced bytes as a Seal and fails, and one refusing an unknown skip-band number fails too. PATH PINNED: libds's `ds_rfcs_record_to` writer, read back in runner.py `_run_rfcs_roundtrip` by libds's reader (`pyds.atoms.iter_atoms`), which yields 260 as a bare field number no `AtomKind` names, and replayed by libds's replayer (`Engine.replay`), which must skip it; the Mercury runtime's `ds.rfcs` writer, read back in compiler/mercury/test/test_behave.m `rfcs_roundtrip_result` by `decode_stream`, whose unknown-number arm skips 260 because `disposition_of_unknown` gives the skip band.
